record.paper_title: Resolving Open Problems on the Euler Sombor Index
record.context_brief: maximal chemical unicyclic graphs for the Euler Sombor index
record.original_question: Let EUS(G) = sum over all edges v_i v_j in E(G) of sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j), where d_i and d_j are the degrees of the endpoints. In chemical graph theory, where molecules are modeled by graphs with vertices representing atoms and edges representing chemical bonds, characterize the unicyclic chemical graphs that attain the maximum Euler Sombor index.

evidence.quote: The Euler Sombor index (EU S) of a graph G is defined as EU S(G) = Σ_{v_i v_j ∈ E(G)} sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j).

Chemical graph theory is an important branch of mathematical chemistry that uses graph theory to represent and study molecular structures. In this approach, molecules are viewed as graphs, where the vertices represent atoms, and the edges represent chemical bonds.
This result provides a complete solution to Open Problem 3 from [24] concerning the minimal graph. However, the corresponding problem for the maximal case remains unresolved.

However, some key problems remain open: determining the maximum EU S index and characterizing the extremal graphs among connected graphs with fixed order and given girth; finding the minimum EU S index and identifying the extremal graphs when both the order and number of pendent vertices are specified; and characterizing the maximal chemical unicyclic graphs for the EU S index.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph $G=(V,E)$, let $d_i$ denote the degree of vertex $v_i$. Define the Euler–Sombor index of $G$ by
$$\mathrm{EUS}(G)=\sum_{v_iv_j\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_i^{2}+d_j^{2}+d_id_j}.$$
A connected graph is called unicyclic if it contains exactly one cycle, equivalently, if $|E(G)|=|V(G)|$. A graph is called chemical if every vertex has degree at most $4$ (modeling molecular structures in which vertices represent atoms and edges represent chemical bonds).

Problem: Among all chemical unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, determine the maximum value of $\mathrm{EUS}(G)$ and characterize all graphs that attain this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works have resolved this problem. A paper titled "Proof of an open problem on the maximization of the Euler–Sombor index in chemical unicyclic graphs" (Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, 2026) provides a complete characterization of the maximizing chemical unicyclic graphs, along with related papers in MDPI Axioms (2025) and AIMS Mathematics (2025) treating extremal unicyclic graphs for the Euler Sombor index.

status_evidence.title: Proof of an open problem on the maximization of the Euler–Sombor index in chemical unicyclic graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A complete characterization of the maximizing problem and identification of the corresponding extremal graphs was subsequently presented.
status_evidence.claim: The maximization problem for the Euler–Sombor index over chemical unicyclic graphs has been solved.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Unicyclic Graphs for the Euler Sombor Index
status_evidence.snippet: The minimum and maximum of the Euler Sombor index for unicyclic graphs with given girth were determined and the corresponding extremal graphs were characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Extremal unicyclic graphs for the Euler Sombor index have been characterized in subsequent literature.

status_evidence.title: Extremal unicyclic and bicyclic graphs of the Euler Sombor index
status_evidence.snippet: Maximal and minimal values of Euler Sombor index for all unicyclic and bicyclic graphs are determined, and the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Extremal results for unicyclic graphs with respect to the Euler Sombor index are known.
